items.prompt: Why can decreasing h worsen a numerical derivative?

options.text: Truncation always increases as h decreases
A smaller h guarantees exact arithmetic
options.why: Floating operations and function evaluations can still be inexact.

options.text: All finite differences are inconsistent formulas
options.why: The problem is not that smooth exact limits always fail.

options.text: Evaluation error is divided by h, and x+h may equal x
options.why: Both amplification and representability need checks.

items.explanation: The complete error budget includes evaluation uncertainty and floating representability, not only truncation.
